diagnostic_evidence.quote: Suppose $(\sigma_k, u_k)$ be an eigenpair to the Steklov EVP~\eqref{eqn: steklov} with $k\geq 1$ so that $\sigma_k > 0$.

issues.failure_explanation:
The proof derives $u_k|_{\partial\Omega} =  rac{1}{\sigma_k}\Lambda\partial_
u u_k$ from Lemma l:NtD and the Steklov condition. But $\Lambda\partial_
u u_k = u_k|_{\partial\Omega}$ by the definition of $\Lambda$ (zero-mean Neumann-to-Dirichlet map, and $u_k$ has zero mean for $\sigma_k>0$). Substituting gives $u_k|_{\partial\Omega} =  rac{1}{\sigma_k}u_k|_{\partial\Omega}$, requiring $\sigma_k = 1$. The correct relation is $u_k|_{\partial\Omega} = \Lambda\partial_
u u_k$. The subsequent proof step silently drops the $1/\sigma_k$ and uses the correct relation, making the argument internally inconsistent. Additionally, the forward direction is restricted to $\sigma_k > 0$ and never addresses the trivial eigenpair $\sigma_k = 0$ with constant $u_k$, despite the theorem claiming 'if and only if' for all eigenpairs.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove the spurious $1/\sigma_k$ factor from the derived formula to read $u_k|_{\partial\Omega} = \Lambda\partial_\nu u_k$, and add one sentence handling $\sigma_k = 0$ (constant eigenfunction maps to constant density $\phi_k$).
issues.overall_effect: The forward direction of Theorem thm: steklov is not rigorously established: the key derived formula is wrong and the case $\sigma_k = 0$ is uncovered. The subsequent reasoning implicitly uses the correct relation, so the result is salvageable.
issues.title: Erroneous Neumann-to-Dirichlet relation and missing zero-eigenvalue case in Steklov proof
issues.why_classification: The erroneous formula is contradicted by the definition of $\Lambda$ and the proof continues with the correct relation; the missing case is trivially fillable. Both fixes are local and preserve every claim.

issues.failure_explanation:
The definition eqn: complex double layer uses $|d\xi|$ (arc-length) in the first integral instead of $d\xi$ (complex line element). The proof of Lemma lem: Complex layer(1) derives $\mathcal{D}[\phi] = \Re[\int( rac{1}{2\pi i}(\zeta-\eta_1)+ rac{\Im(z-\xi)}{b})\phi\,d\xi]$ with $d\xi$ and then equates it to $\Re f_\mathcal{D}[\phi]$ as defined with $|d\xi|$, an invalid inference. Since $d\xi = i
u|d\xi|$, the real part of $\int(\zeta-\eta_1)\phi\,d\xi/(2\pi i)$ is $\int\Re[
u(\zeta-\eta_1)]\phi|d\xi|/(2\pi)$, which differs from $\int\Im(\zeta-\eta_1)\phi|d\xi|/(2\pi)$ (the real part of the $|d\xi|$ version) for general $
u$. Likewise, the Sokhotski-Plemelj jump in part (2) requires a Cauchy integral with $d\i$; with $|d\xi|$ the jump is $i\phi ar
u$ rather than $\mp\phi/2$.

failure_location.quote: In fact, $\Re  f_\mathcal{D}[\phi] = \mathcal{D}[\phi]$, which is a function on $\mathbb T_\tau\backslash\partial\Omega$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change $|d\xi|$ to $d\xi$ in the first integral of eqn: complex double layer and in the Sokhotski-Plemelj step of the proof of part (2). With this correction $f_\mathcal{D}$ is analytic, $\Re f_\mathcal{D} = \mathcal{D}$, and the jump holds by the standard Sokhotski-Plemelj formula; all downstream proofs then work as intended.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma lem: Complex layer parts (1) and (2) are false with the stated definition. Proofs of Lemma lem: properties double layer(4)-(5) and Lemma lem: characteristic(2) rely on $\Re f_\mathcal{D} = \mathcal{D}$ and the jump relation and are therefore unreliable. Theorem thm: dirichlet depends on these lemmas.
issues.title: Complex double-layer potential defined with arc-length instead of complex line element
issues.why_classification: The repair is a single-measure change ($|d\xi| \to d\xi$) in one definition and one proof step. All proofs already use properties that hold with $d\xi$, so no new lemma or construction is needed and every guarantee is preserved.

issues.failure_explanation: The continuous eigenproblem is $(\mathcal{D}^* + \frac{1}{2}I)(I-\mathcal{M})\phi = \sigma\mathcal{S}_0[\phi]$ with $\mathcal{S}_0[\phi] = \mathcal{S}[(I-\mathcal{M})\phi] + \mathcal{M}\phi$. Its discrete form is $(D_s + \frac{1}{2}I)(I-M)\vec\phi = \sigma[S(I-M) + M]\vec\phi$ because $M\vec\phi = \bar\phi\mathbf{1}$ supplies the constant $\bar\phi$ in $\mathcal{S}_0$. The stated discrete equation uses $\sigma S(I-M)\vec\phi$ on the right, omitting $\sigma M\vec\phi$. For $\sigma > 0$ the eigenfunction $u = \mathcal{S}_0[\phi] = \mathcal{S}\psi + \bar\phi$ then satisfies $\partial_\nu u = \sigma\mathcal{S}\psi \neq \sigma u$ unless $\bar\phi = 0$. Eigenvalues remain correct (the equation constrains only $\psi = (I-M)\vec\phi$), but the eigenfunction formula and the stated eigenproblem are inconsistent.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the matrix $M$ to the right-hand side: $(D_s + \frac{1}{2}I)(I-M)\vec\phi = \sigma[S(I-M) + M]\vec\phi$, which is consistent with $\mathcal{S}_0 = \mathcal{S}(I-\mathcal{M}) + \mathcal{M}$ and restores correct eigenfunctions.
issues.overall_effect: The discrete Steklov eigenproblem as written produces eigenfunctions that fail $\partial_\nu u_k = \sigma_k u_k$ by a constant $\sigma_k\bar\phi$. Eigenvalues are correct. The formula $u = \mathcal{S}_0[\phi]$ is inconsistent with the eigenproblem and can yield wrong eigenfunctions depending on the eigenvector normalization chosen by MATLAB's eig.
issues.title: Discrete Steklov eigenproblem omits the $\sigma M\vec\phi$ term from $\mathcal{S}_0$
issues.why_classification: The error is in the algorithm specification and affects the computed output (eigenfunctions). The fix requires understanding the $\mathcal{S}_0$ decomposition to identify the missing term and a choice between two repairs (add $M$ to the RHS or change the eigenfunction formula to $\mathcal{S}\psi$). The fix is contained but not purely typographical.
